transcript: Last night, Marie and I saw The Outsiders on Broadway and we really enjoyed it. Neither of us had read the book, Marie knew some of the basic plot points but we were going in with pretty fresh eyes. I'm not sure I'm sold on the story itself but I was very sold on this production. Every musical on Broadway has great singers and this one is no different but what I loved about this one was how much the score showcased the vocals, particularly Brody Grant who plays Ponyboy — he has such a resonant, aching, and emotional tone. I thought the lyrics were alright but the music was really strong, definitely up there for me in terms of new scores these days. One minor quibble I had sonically which I hope tightens up a bit before the opening night is that the sound mixing and the balance, at least from where we were sitting, was a little rough at times and the vocals and harmonies could have been crisper in the mix. Another strength of this musical is the action sequences, specifically there's one involving rain in Act 2 which is a really impressive blend of movement, sound, lighting, and projection. Overall we thought it was a very captivating piece, and I'd recommend it whether or not you’ve read the book. But just as a side note, if you're not familiar with the story, there's a fair amount of physical violence and it's pretty realistically done here which is either really cool or maybe a bit much depending on how you feel about it. With that, another playbill for my collection.
